youtube.title: They Were Told to Put Radioactive Paint in Their Mouths | The Radium Girls
youtube.description:
In the late 1910s, hundreds of young women at the U.S. Radium Corporation in Orange, New Jersey painted watch dials with radium paint, shaping their brushes with their lips. The company called the paint harmless while its chemists used lead screens and tongs. Grace Fryer and four others sued in 1927; the 1928 settlement came too late, and the case helped establish workers' right to sue over occupational disease.

📂 Case File #040: The Radium Girls
